items.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005
items.q: So anyway I came the next day and I played for Jones and he hired me.

ctx.x: Was that what they called a cafeteria style?

Yeah. It was a cafeteria. So anyway I came the next day and I played for Jones and he hired me. But the guys didn’t like me. You know why they didn’t like me? They wanted away from Jones, Jones hires me, he didn’t need me, but he only used me to solo here and there. You know who was the arranger? He became big later. Gordon Jenkins. Gordon Jenkins was the arranger. So I stayed with him until let’s say around July 7th or 8th, until after Labor Day. We toured all of New England with Jones. It was cold. There were…

items.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995
items.q: and Ish hired me but the guys didn’t like me.

ctx.x: When I left New Orleans I was headed for New York. But I stopped in Philadelphia because a fine trumpet player from New Orleans, Danny Ryan, was in Philadelphia. So I go up to the rooming house and a lady opened the door and she says, “Oh, Danny is playing in Ocean City” with a certain band. I went there and Danny said that Adrian Fleiss was a violin player from New Orleans, was playing with the George Olson band in Atlantic City at the Ritz Carlton. I go there but Olson had just left. And this is a true story. I…

come here tomorrow, Ish is rehearsing” and so forth. I went there the next day with my alto, clarinet and I had baritone with me, and Ish hired me but the guys didn’t like me. You know why? They all wanted a raise. They wanted a raise.
Oh, they didn’t want another player.
